# dataset — spec

## Maturity

**Grade:** 3 · S2 E2 A2 H1 P3 · limited by performance (not measured) *(generated by `zig build gen-catalog`)*

**Scope:** parity — Apache Arrow / pandas table model at dashboard scale: typed columns, nulls, exact decimals, dates and UTC instants, self-describing wire and JSON; the columnar engine, Arrow IPC/Parquet, tz-aware and nested types are consciously rejected (see Compared with) (surveyed 2026-11-02)

**Audit:** review 2026-10-04 · mutation 2026-10-04 (42/43, 1 eq) · src ?

**Hardening:** fuzz 2026-11-02 (`DATASET_FUZZ=200000` on 2 disjoint seed ranges, 400k seeds clean, ReleaseSafe, reach labels accepted, round_tripped, truncated, rejected; rerun after the chunked decoder) · ct n/a — tabular data handling (keyword review, 2026-10-07) · panic 2026-10-31 (sweep + blind review: exact int/float/decimal order (strict weak order for `std.sort`), `cell`/`floatColumn`/`seriesXY` total, `appendRow` checked panic; delta audit 28/30 + 2 eq)

**Performance:** not measured

**Evidence:** model — golden wire vector + round-trip over random timestamps 0000..9999; fuzz is never-panic only

**Known defects:** none recorded

**Downstream consumer:** yes

Canonical in-memory columnar-typed table — the seam between data sources and consumers. Usage: see
./README.md. Attribution/provenance: see this module's README "Provenance" note — clean-room, so there is deliberately no root `/NOTICE` entry to point at (root `NOTICE` §0).

**Where we are ahead:** the only Zig table type that comes with a verb algebra (`tabular`), stats
(`finstats`) and JSON/CSV feeds in the same collection; an exact `.decimal` (i128, 12 digits)
column with exact compare and exact JSON output — Arrow has decimal128 but pandas/polars users
usually fall back to float *(inferred)*; a bounds-checked wire format with a fixed
golden vector, verified under a big-endian target; a microsecond UTC `.timestamp` with an
RFC 3339 parser/formatter in the container itself. **Where we are behind** (re-checked
2026-10-04): no typed columnar layout (documented ceiling), no timezone-aware timestamps,
list/struct or categorical type, no validity-bitmap or zero-copy interchange with Arrow/Parquet
(→ Backlog). Why this is still "core": the reference's *table model* — typed columns, nulls,
exact decimals, dates and instants, a self-describing interchange — is all here at the scale the
consumers run (dashboard-sized results, wgs); what is missing is the columnar *engine*, which
is a different representation, not a missing feature of this one.

**Verdict per gap (2026-11-02).** *Typed columnar layout and zero-copy column reads:* rejected as a
change (the measured cost against Arrow is decode 1.7x and `floatColumn` 3.3x; a columnar `Dataset` breaks every
consumer that indexes `rows`: wgs, `tabular`, `jsonshape`, `finstats`) and kept as the Backlog item.
*Arrow IPC / Parquet interchange:* rejected for now. A user feeding pandas/polars would notice it,
but no consumer does (wgs uses the private wire as a cache and `toJson` for the UI; CSV/JSON siblings
cover export); it needs a columnar view first and a flatbuffers metadata writer/reader (est. 1.5k
lines, an estimate), no sibling module owns it, and pyarrow, the natural oracle, is not installed
here. *Timezone-aware timestamps, list/struct/dictionary types:* rejected (no tz database in a leaf
container; no consumer). *Validity bitmaps:* a representation detail of the columnar layout.
*Compute kernels:* owned by `tabular` and `finstats`.

## Design & invariants
- Every origin normalizes to one shape: `{ columns: [{name,type}], rows: [[Value…]] }`; consumers
  never see a source schema, only a `Dataset`. `ColumnType`: int/float/text/bool/date/decimal/timestamp. `Value`
  is a tagged union with `asFloat`/`asInt`/`asText`/`isNull`/`eql`/`order`/`cast`.
- `.decimal` (`ColumnType`) / `Value.decimal: i128` — exact fixed-point money/quantity type. Stores
  a RAW `i128` at `decimal_scale = 1_000_000_000_000` (12 fractional digits), the exact convention of
  the sibling `decimal` module's `Decimal{ .raw }`. **No dependency on `decimal`** — `dataset` stays a
  leaf container; consumers wrap the raw value themselves as `decimal.Decimal{ .raw = value.decimal }`
  for arithmetic/formatting. `eql`/`order` compare two decimals exactly on the raw `i128` (not the
  lossy `asFloat` path used for cross-type numeric comparison). `cast(.decimal)` handles int/float
  widening (float path returns `null` on non-finite input); text→decimal is NOT attempted (would need
  the `decimal` module's parser). `toJson` emits an exact placed-point number literal (integer math,
  scale-derived decimal point, trailing zeros trimmed) — never the lossy f64 path `.float` uses. The
  binary wire format got a new tag (`5`, appended after the existing `0..4`, not inserted) so
  already-serialized data never renumbers.
- `Builder` — incremental row-at-a-time `Dataset` construction (`init(allocator, columns)` →
  `appendRow(cells)` → `toOwned()`) for sources that don't know their row count up front, without
  pre-sizing an array.
- **Memory model: a `Dataset` is an immutable view.** Transforms are `dataset → dataset`: take an
  allocator (normally a caller-owned arena for the whole pipeline) and return a **new** `Dataset`.
  Structural arrays (`columns`, `rows`, per-row `Value` slices) are allocated from that allocator;
  text payloads may be borrowed from the input (safe since nothing is ever mutated in place) or
  freshly allocated. Free everything at once via the arena — no piecemeal free.
- `Date.ordinal()` uses Howard Hinnant's days-from-civil algorithm (proleptic Gregorian, 1970-01-01
  = 0) with `@divFloor` for the era (Hinnant's `y - 399` form assumes C's truncating division; with a
  flooring one it misplaced years −400..−2 by one era — fixed 2026-10-04). `Date.fromOrdinal` is the
  inverse (civil-from-days); a day-by-day walk over 2 000 001 days checks each step against the
  calendar rule, not against the code. Proleptic: no Julian calendar before 1582.
- `.timestamp` (appended 2026-10-04, wire column byte 6): cells are `Value.int` microseconds since
  1970-01-01T00:00:00Z. **Why reuse `.int` instead of a new `Value` variant:** a new variant breaks
  every exhaustive `switch` over `Value` in consumers (wgs has one, `decimalx.zig` `keyString`) and
  adds a wire value tag; `.date` already set the pattern (column tag = intent, cell = existing
  variant). **Why microseconds:** PostgreSQL's and DuckDB's `TIMESTAMP` unit and Arrow's
  `timestamp[us]`; an i64 spans ±292 000 years, so every 4-digit-year input fits (no overflow path
  in the parser: |result| ≤ ~2.6e17). `parseIsoTimestamp` grammar is in its doc comment; a missing
  zone is UTC (Arrow's tz-naive convention); `:60` and `24:00` are refused (Python's
  `fromisoformat` refuses both). `formatIsoTimestamp` is total over i64 (expanded years outside
  0000–9999; anchors: numpy's `datetime64[us]` limits `+294247-01-10T04:00:54.775807` /
  `-290308-12-21T19:59:05.224192`). `toJson` renders a `.timestamp` column's int cells as RFC 3339
  strings (unambiguous unit; a row longer than the schema renders its extra cells untyped).
- `parseIsoDate` (tightened 2026-10-04): four/two/two ASCII digits — `std.fmt.parseInt` accepted a
  sign, so `"2024-+1-01"` was January — and the day must exist in its month.
- Serialize/deserialize is a compact binary wire format with exact round-trip (`error.Corrupt` on
  truncation/bad tag) plus a JSON projection (non-finite float → null). **Explicit little-endian on
  the wire, independent of host byte order** — every multi-byte field (`u32` lengths, `i64`/`f64`
  cells, `i128` decimal cells) goes through `std.mem.writeInt`/`readInt(..., .little)`, not
  `std.mem.toBytes`/`bytesToValue` (which write/read the host's *native* representation — silently
  correct on every little-endian CI lane, silently wrong cross-endian). Floats are bit-cast to their
  same-width integer before the explicit-endian write, then bit-cast back on read — the IEEE-754 bit
  *pattern* is host-independent, only its byte order is, so this is correct on a big-endian host too.
  A fixed golden byte vector (computed independently, outside this module, with Python's
  `struct.pack('<...')`) pins the documented little-endian contract; a same-process round-trip cannot
  — encode and decode agree with each other regardless of which byte order either one actually uses.
  Cross-verified by running the suite under `qemu-s390x` against a `-Dtarget=s390x-linux-musl`
  (big-endian) build. On a little-endian host the wire bytes are unchanged by this fix — verified
  byte-for-byte against the golden vector — so no existing little-endian-host payload (e.g. a
  consumer's on-disk cache) is invalidated.
- **Known ceiling, by design:** row-major, boxed-`Value` representation (each cell a tagged union,
  each row a slice of them) — simple and allocator-friendly, not a typed columnar layout. No
  SIMD-friendly per-column scans or Arrow-style memory density; fine for dashboard-sized result sets,
  not a multi-million-row analytical engine.
- `serialize` makes one pass over the cells (row length summed while the row is hot, buffer grown per row, plain stores; initial capacity guessed from the first row) and `deserialize` carves the per-row `Value` arrays from chunks of 256 rows; wire bytes are unchanged (golden vector). Short texts are copied into 16 KiB slabs, not one allocation each (profile: `ArenaAllocator.alloc` was as large as the decode loop). Measured 2026-11-02, per 20 000 x 6 table: encode 595 -> ~530 us, decode 880 -> ~400 us.
- Pure logic, no OS calls, reentrant, no shared state.

## Threat model / out of scope
Not a security boundary — an in-memory data-shape primitive over caller-supplied or caller-parsed
data. `deserialize` treats untrusted bytes defensively (bounds-checked, `error.Corrupt` on
truncation/bad tag/length overflow, never a panic or OOB read) since a wire round-trip may cross a
process or cache boundary. **The `ncol`/`nrow` guards bound the wire counts, not the resulting
memory** — accepted input grows into a **~48×** larger `Dataset` (measured flat at 48.0–48.1× from
64 KB to 8 MB input, worst case `ncol = 1`: `@sizeOf(Value)` = 32 B plus a 16 B/row slice header
against a 1 B/cell wire minimum). A caller sizing an untrusted-input budget must size it around
this factor, not around `bytes.len` — see the doc comment on `deserialize`. `Value.order` treats
NaN as the greatest value and NaN == NaN (both floats reach `order` unfiltered from wire tag `2`
with no finiteness check — see the doc comment on `Value.order`). `Date.ordinal` is not a certified
calendar-math primitive (see Design & invariants) — do not use it for legal/financial date arithmetic
requiring exact historical calendar correctness.

## Verification
`zig build test-dataset` (+ `-Doptimize=ReleaseFast`; `zig fmt --check modules/dataset`):
`Value` coercion/comparison/ordering (`asFloat`/`asInt`/`cast`/`eql`/`order` incl. null<bool<numeric<
text, and `decimal`'s exact-raw-i128 compare/coercion), `Dataset` accessors (`columnIndex`/
`columnType`/`cell`/`floatColumn`/`seriesXY`), `concat` (same-schema append + `error.SchemaMismatch`),
binary serialize/deserialize round-trip + corruption rejection (incl. the new `decimal` wire tag), a
fixed little-endian golden byte vector asserted byte-for-byte against `serialize`'s output and fed to
`deserialize` (cross-checked live under `qemu-s390x`, `-Dtarget=s390x-linux-musl`), `toJson` shape
(incl. non-finite float → null, exact placed-point `decimal`), `parseIsoDate` +
`Date.ordinal` monotonic ordering, `Builder` incremental construction; `.timestamp`: published
Unix-time anchors (946684800, 1234567890, 2147483647, 253402300799), offsets/fractions/separators,
a refusal list for the grammar's edges, a 20 000-sample format→parse round trip, the i64 limits as
numpy prints them, `Date.fromOrdinal` against a day-by-day calendar walk, `cast`/`toJson`/wire.

## Backlog / deferred

- **A performance reference that covers encode and decode** *(bench 2026-11-02, why the card says `not measured`)*: `zig build bench-dataset -Djcc-safe`, 20 000 rows x 6 columns, 9 rounds, under load, spread up to 87 %. The like-for-like row model, Go gota v0.12.0, has no wire format and no nullable row builder, so it pairs only two of seven ops: `col_f64` 0.26×, `col_text` 0.08×. wgs uses this module for encode, decode and JSON, so a P2 from those two rows would claim what they do not show. Against Apache Arrow Go v18.8.0 (typed columnar, the fastest measured; arrow-rs and nanoarrow not built): `build` 0.30×, `encode` 1.02×, `decode` 1.66×, `col_f64` 3.29×, `col_i64` 1.04×, `col_text` 1.14×, `col_misc` 1.14×; formats differ, private wire vs Arrow IPC stream. `col_f64` is the 32-byte cell and a cache line per row: closing it takes a columnar layout, which is breaking, or an additive numeric column read, not tried.
- **Foreign code of the bench** *(2026-11-02)*: arrow-go and gota were compiled after `go list -deps` showed no cgo, os/exec, net or plugin in either graph; their source was not read. Arrow is an Apache project; gota is less well known and its own 9.8k lines were swept for exec, network, cgo and init (clean), not read.
- **Worst ratio against the fastest is 3.3x (`floatColumn` vs a typed slice), decode 1.7x, because of the boxed row-major layout** *(2026-11-02)*: Before the 2026-11-02 fixes decode was 2.5x. What is left is the 32-byte cell plus one cache line per row visited by a column read; only a typed columnar `Dataset` (breaking, see Compared with) closes it. An additive column cache or `floatColumn` fast path was not tried. `fastest` is Arrow Go; arrow-rs and nanoarrow are unmeasured. The reference (gota) covers only the column reads, so the encode/decode/build rows have no row-model reference at all (searched: gota, dataframe-go; none has a wire format).
- **Zig 0.17: a wide `@bitCast` on a possibly hot path** *(2026-10-19, `~/CML/zig-017/bitcast-scan/REPORT.md`)* — 0.17 lowers a `@bitCast` between `[N]u8` (N > 8) and a wider-element type (here: `i128`) to a per-byte loop (~8x the instructions; codeberg ziglang/zig #36256): `i128v`, `Out.i128v` (per i128 value). Measure first (cycles + instructions 0.16 vs 0.17, or the cast's share in a profile); fix only if it shows: load/store through `*align(1) uN` + `std.mem.nativeToBig`/`bigToNative` (identical bytes, 8 instructions).

- **`deserialize` memory amplification has no caller-set cap** *(no-panic sweep GW, 2026-10-31)*:
  an accepted document costs up to 48x its wire size (`@sizeOf(Value)` 32 B per 1-byte cell, 16 B row
  headers), documented on `deserialize`; the module bounds the COUNTS the bytes can prove, not the
  result. A consumer reading untrusted blobs must cap `bytes.len` itself. Fix needs new API
  (`deserializeLimited(a, bytes, max_cells)` or a limit struct), hence not done in the sweep.

From README "Deferred (backlog, not implemented here)":
- **True columnar storage** (typed per-column arrays, SIMD-friendly layout) — a different
  representation entirely; big perf-engineering investment with no current high-throughput product
  driving the need (dashboard-sized result sets are the actual workload). Per the library's
  perf-investment policy, deferred until a consumer's throughput actually demands it.
- ~~`.decimal` `ColumnType`/`Value` variant~~ — **done**: raw `i128` inline, no dependency on
  `decimal` (see Design & invariants above).
- ~~Streaming/chunked construction~~ — **done**: `Builder`.
- ~~`distinct`/dedup at the dataset level~~ — **not duplicated here**: covered by
  `tabular.distinct` (added this cycle), which already owns the group-key/keep-first-or-last design.

`dataset` is the anchor of a sibling family already extracted (`tabular` = dataset algebra,
`jsonshape` = JSON→dataset projection) — those are separate modules, not gaps in this one.

- ~~**Date-time (timestamp) column type**~~ *(survey 2026-09-30; done, see the struck entry below)*: `ColumnType` had `date` (y/m/d) but no
  instant with time-of-day or zone, which every dataframe library has; sub-daily data
  (ticks, logs) must go through int/text. Effort M (new tag appended on the wire, like `.decimal`).
  Fits §2.
- **Arrow IPC (or another standard) interchange** *(survey 2026-09-30)*: the only serialization is
  the private binary format and JSON; nothing else can read a `Dataset`. Effort L (would need a
  columnar view, see next). Fits §2 (Arrow IPC is a documented format; a sibling module).
- ~~Date-time (timestamp) column type~~ — **done 2026-10-04**: `.timestamp`, UTC microseconds (see
  Design & invariants). Still deferred: **timezone-aware timestamps** (zone per column, wall-clock
  rendering) — needs a tz database, which a leaf container should not carry; consumers convert at
  the edge. Arrow IPC (above) stays deferred: it needs the columnar view first.
- True columnar storage is already listed above (Known ceiling); the survey confirms it is what
  separates this module from every reference above, and that it blocks interchange.

- **2026-10-19 — Zig 0.17.0 miscompile #37131 (signed → narrower unsigned cast emits `trunc nsw`; upper-half values are poison in ReleaseSafe/ReleaseFast)**

## Status
`extract · any · util · reentrant` + deps: none — canonical source is `pub const meta` in
src/root.zig.

## Anchoring

**Anchor grade:** class C · oracle n/a

- **Class C** — internal algorithm or data structure — no outside exists, so correctness is defined by invariants or a brute-force reference. Not anchor debt.
- **Oracle n/a** — class C/D carries no anchor debt, so there is no oracle grade to give.

**What the tests actually contain.** internal tabular Value/Dataset abstraction, plus one wire-format
oracle: the little-endian golden byte vector above. It pins this module's own documented on-wire
contract (there is no external spec/RFC for it), so it does not change the Class C grade — it is a
brute-force reference for our own invariant, not an outside conformance target. The calendar and
`.timestamp` tests (2026-10-04) are pinned to published values — Unix-time anchors, numpy's
`datetime64[us]` limits, Python's ordinal of 0001-01-01 — and to the calendar rule itself (a
day-by-day walk), not to this module's output.
